summary: Go ListMcpResourcesTool has the same canonical name, a compatible visible server parameter, concurrency-safe marking, and deferred-discovery metadata, but it is not behaviorally aligned with the TS reference. The largest gaps are runtime logic and output contract: Go's all-server path lists configured servers and cached tools instead of resources, the cached connected-server path can return tools without calling resources/list, and the real resources/list path returns a raw MCP envelope rather than the TS flat resource array with an injected server field. Go also lacks TS-equivalent capabilities gating, non-connected client-state semantics, per-server failure isolation, resource cache/reconnect/list_changed lifecycle, read-only/result-size metadata, and focused parity tests.

gaps.title: All-server and cached-connected paths list tools/configs instead of MCP resources
gaps.description: TS ListMcpResourcesTool always works in terms of MCP resources: without a server it processes all current MCP clients and returns resources from all connected clients; with a server it filters to that server and fetches its resources. Go's no-server path only prints configured server names and cached tools. Go's specific-server path also returns cached tools whenever a ready connection has any tool cache, which is the normal production state after Connect() calls tools/list, so a server with both tools and resources can never reach resources/list through that branch.

ts_evidence.note: call() selects clients, ensures connected clients, calls fetchResourcesForClient, and returns results.flat().
The prompt says omitting server returns resources from all servers.

go_evidence.note: listAll() renders configured server names and cached tool descriptions; it never calls resources/list.
listOne() returns cached tools for any ready real connection with len(conn.tools) > 0.
Connect() populates conn.tools from tools/list before storing the ready connection, making the cached-tools branch common.
The current ListAll test asserts server names, not resource aggregation.

gaps.impact: Model-visible behavior is wrong for the main advertised operation: resource discovery can show MCP tools instead of resources and all-server resource discovery is effectively absent.

gaps.title: Go returns prose or a raw resources envelope instead of the TS flat resource array with server fields
gaps.description: TS declares the output as an array of resource objects containing uri, name, optional mimeType, optional description, and required server. fetchResourcesForClient injects server into each resource, and mapToolResultToToolResultBlockParam serializes the array itself. Go returns plain prose for listAll/cached paths and returns the raw MCP result object {"resources":[...]} for real resources/list. The raw envelope omits the TS-injected server field and changes the top-level JSON shape from array to object.

ts_evidence.note: outputSchema is a flat array of resource objects with required server.
fetchResourcesForClient requests resources/list and maps each resource to include server: client.name.
The tool result block serializes the flat output array, with a special no-resources message only for empty content.
The UI renderer pretty-prints the output array.

go_evidence.note: Go ToolResult is string Content plus optional metadata/content blocks, with no typed ListMcpResources output object.
listAll() builds human-readable text.
The real resources/list branch returns raw JSON from the MCP server, or {"resources":[]} for empty raw output.
Current parity tests assert a top-level resources envelope, not the TS flat array with server fields.

gaps.impact: Consumers or tests expecting the TS output schema must special-case Go, and the model loses the server provenance field that TS guarantees.

gaps.title: Go does not model TS connected/failed/needs-auth/pending/disabled client states for resource listing
gaps.description: TS receives a runtime mcpClients array whose union type includes connected, failed, needs-auth, pending, and disabled clients. ListMcpResourcesTool only fetches from connected clients; non-connected clients contribute an empty list, and a target server that exists but is not connected does not force a fresh spawn from config inside the tool. Go MCPManager tracks only configs plus ready connections, so listOne attempts Connect() for a configured server and returns IsError when connection or tools/list fails. That is a broader lifecycle side effect and a different model-visible result.

ts_evidence.note: MCPServerConnection is a union of connected, failed, needs-auth, pending, and disabled states; ServerResource adds server.
Per-client processing skips non-connected clients and catches per-client errors as empty results.
The connection manager owns MCP state updates and clears tools/commands/resources when clients become disabled or failed.

go_evidence.note: MCPManager stores configs and active server connections, not failed/needs-auth/pending/disabled runtime states.
Connect() attempts to start/connect the configured server and fails the tool path on connection or tools/list errors.
listOne() returns an IsError ToolResult when Connect() fails.
SetupRegistry loads settings directly into MCPManager and registers ListMcpResourcesTool against that config/connection manager.

gaps.impact: The Go tool can start processes or surface errors in cases where TS would operate over already-managed runtime client state and return an empty resource list for non-connected clients.

gaps.title: Capabilities gating and per-server failure isolation are incomplete
gaps.description: TS only calls resources/list when a connected client advertises capabilities.resources, and any resources/list error is logged and converted to an empty result so one bad server does not sink the whole list. Go's tool-layer path has no resource capability check; it calls resources/list directly and returns IsError on failure. The lower-level Go services/mcp client has structured capabilities and resource types, but ListMcpResourcesTool uses the older mcp.Client surface that does not retain initialize capabilities.

ts_evidence.note: fetchResourcesForClient returns [] when resources capability is absent and catches/logs failures.
ListMcpResourcesTool wraps every client fetch in try/catch and returns [] for that server on failure.

go_evidence.note: ListMcpResourcesTool calls resources/list with CallRaw and converts any error into an IsError result.
The mcp.Client initialize path sends capabilities but this client struct does not expose stored server capabilities.
mcp.Client.ListResources calls resources/list directly without capability gating.
A newer services/mcp client already stores initialize capabilities, but the tool manager does not use it.
The services/mcp client also has structured ListResourcesResult/ListResources helpers that could support a typed implementation.

gaps.impact: Servers without resource support, temporarily broken resources/list handlers, or mixed healthy/unhealthy server sets produce Go errors instead of TS-style empty per-server results.

gaps.title: Resource cache, reconnect, and resources/list_changed semantics do not match TS
gaps.description: TS documents and implements an LRU resource cache keyed by server name, warmed during MCP startup, invalidated on connection close and resources/list_changed notifications, and refreshed via ensureConnectedClient before listing. Go currently has no resource cache for ListMcpResourcesTool, and the resources/list_changed handler only sets an informational dirty flag that the tool does not consume. Go also lacks an onclose-driven resource cache invalidation path equivalent to TS because the tool path is not backed by the same cached resource fetch layer.

ts_evidence.note: The TS tool comments state resources are LRU-cached, warmed at startup, invalidated on onclose/list_changed, and reconnected before fetch.
onclose clears fetchResourcesForClient cache and the connection cache.
ensureConnectedClient reconnects by using connectToServer when the cache was cleared.
resources/list_changed deletes the resource cache and updates server resources.

go_evidence.note: The Go notification comment says the resources-changed flag is informational because resource lists are not cached.
ResourcesChanged/ConsumeResourcesChanged exist, but no ListMcpResourcesTool path consumes them.
resources/list_changed only flips a flag and calls an optional invalidator; it does not refresh resources.
ListMcpResourcesTool.Execute/listOne contain no cache lookup, dirty-flag consumption, or reconnect-on-close invalidation logic.

gaps.impact: Go lacks TS's stable resource freshness model and cannot prove that listings after close/list_changed avoid stale data or gracefully reconnect.

gaps.title: Read-only, result-size, output-schema, and classifier metadata are not represented at the Go tool boundary
gaps.description: The TS tool declares isReadOnly=true, shouldDefer=true, a searchHint, maxResultSizeChars=100000, outputSchema, toAutoClassifierInput, and isResultTruncated. Go marks concurrency safe and has registry-level deferred metadata, but the core Tool interface has no read-only hook, output schema, per-tool max result size, result truncation predicate, or auto-classifier input. This is partly framework-wide, but it directly affects ListMcpResourcesTool parity because TS treats this as a read-only, bounded, structured-output discovery tool.

ts_evidence.note: TS declares concurrency safety, read-only status, classifier input, shouldDefer, searchHint, and maxResultSizeChars.
TS exposes inputSchema and outputSchema.
TS detects result truncation using jsonStringify(output).
The TS Tool contract includes outputSchema, isReadOnly, shouldDefer, and maxResultSizeChars.

go_evidence.note: Go ListMcpResourcesTool exposes name, alias, concurrency, description, and input schema only.
Go Tool interface only requires Name, Description, Schema, and Execute.
Deferred metadata exists via a registry map for ListMcpResourcesTool/ReadMcpResourceTool, but not read-only/result-size/output-schema metadata.
The repo's architecture notes identify missing isReadOnly and non-uniform result-size handling in Go.
The same notes call out the thin Tool interface and missing unified truncation as high/medium gaps.

gaps.impact: Permission/risk handling and result-budget behavior cannot be made tool-equivalent for ListMcpResourcesTool without either tool-specific metadata extensions or broader framework support.

gaps.title: Go accepts a non-TS server_name alias that is not advertised in the schema
gaps.description: TS exposes and consumes only the optional server field. Go's JSON schema also advertises only server, but parseInput accepts server_name and Execute falls back to it. This may be intentional backward compatibility with older Go tests, but it is not a TS surface and the alias is hidden from the schema, making behavior harder to reason about.

ts_evidence.note: The TS input schema contains only optional server.
TS call() reads input.server as targetServer.

go_evidence.note: Go Schema() advertises only server.
ListMcpResourcesInput also has ServerName json:"server_name".
Execute() falls back from server to server_name.
Current tests explicitly assert parsing server_name.

gaps.impact: The model-facing schema and actual accepted inputs diverge, and tests encourage a non-TS field name.

gaps.title: Current Go tests miss the TS-critical ListMcpResources behaviors and lock in Go-specific behavior
gaps.description: The existing Go tests cover metadata, no-server text, server-name listing, a single-server resources/list happy path only when no tools are cached, and unknown-server IsError. They do not assert all-server resource aggregation, flat array output, injected server fields, the production cached-tools branch, capabilities gating, per-server failure isolation, TS empty-state tool result content, or absence/handling of the server_name alias. The current parity contract also asserts a raw resources envelope, which conflicts with the TS output schema.

ts_evidence.note: The TS output schema is a flat array with server fields.
The TS runtime contract includes all-client fetch, reconnect, error isolation, and flattening.
The TS model-facing mapper has a specific no-resources message and serializes the output array.

go_evidence.note: Tests assert no-server prose/listing and single-server resources only with nil cached tools.
Tests assert raw resources envelope empty handling and unknown-server IsError, but not TS array output.
The parity contract preserves resource envelope fields but still expects a top-level resources object.
Older alignment tests discuss structured output but only check JSON/prose and mimeType, not the current TS flat array plus server field contract.

gaps.impact: A future implementation can pass local tests while remaining incompatible with the TS reference, especially on the most important all-server and cached-connection paths.

candidate_tasks.title: Align ListMcpResourcesTool resource enumeration and output contract
candidate_tasks.objective: Make Go ListMcpResourcesTool fetch MCP resources, not tool caches, and return the TS-compatible flat JSON array of resources with server provenance.
acceptance: Calling ListMcpResourcesTool with no server aggregates resources from all applicable connected/resource-capable servers instead of printing configured server names or tool caches.
Calling it with a specific server calls resources/list even when conn.tools is populated.
Model-facing Content is a JSON array matching TS output shape: each item has uri, name, optional mimeType, optional description, and server.
Empty resource results map to the TS no-resources semantics rather than 'No MCP servers registered.' or '(no tools cached)'.
Existing ReadMcpResourceTool behavior is not regressed.

candidate_tasks.title: Add TS-equivalent MCP resource capability and client-state handling
candidate_tasks.objective: Ensure ListMcpResourcesTool only requests resources/list for servers that are connected and advertise resources support, and mirrors TS's empty-result behavior for non-connected or failed per-server states.
acceptance: MCPServerConn or the client layer retains initialize server capabilities needed to determine resources support.
Servers without capabilities.resources contribute [] instead of receiving a resources/list call.
All-server listing isolates failures per server and still returns resources from healthy servers.

A target server that exists but is failed/needs-auth/pending/disabled does not cause an opportunistic process start from ListMcpResourcesTool; behavior is documented and tested against the TS state model.
Unknown target server still returns a clear error with available server names.

candidate_tasks.title: Implement resource cache, reconnect, and resources/list_changed lifecycle parity
candidate_tasks.objective: Mirror TS fetchResourcesForClient lifecycle: cache resources by server, invalidate on connection close and resources/list_changed, and reconnect/refetch without stale results.
acceptance: Resource listings are cached per server only when that preserves TS freshness semantics.
notifications/resources/list_changed invalidates or refreshes the affected server resource cache and the tool consumes that invalidation.
Closed or unhealthy connections trigger reconnect/refetch before returning cached resource data.
One server's reconnect or refresh failure logs/returns empty for that server without failing aggregate listing.
No stale resource list is returned after a tested resources/list_changed notification.

candidate_tasks.title: Expose ListMcpResourcesTool read-only and result-budget metadata
candidate_tasks.objective: Represent TS tool metadata that affects permissions, classifier input, output typing, and result-size handling for ListMcpResourcesTool.
acceptance: ListMcpResourcesTool can be identified as read-only by the Go permission/risk layer.
ListMcpResourcesTool has a per-tool result-size cap equivalent to TS maxResultSizeChars=100000, or the framework has an explicit documented equivalent.
The tool exposes enough output metadata/tests to assert the TS flat resource-array shape.
Deferred discovery metadata remains present with a search hint at least as specific as the TS hint.
Existing concurrency behavior remains true.

candidate_tasks.title: Resolve the non-TS server_name input alias
candidate_tasks.objective: Make the accepted input surface explicit and TS-aligned: advertise and prefer only server, or deliberately retain server_name as a documented legacy alias outside the model-facing schema.
acceptance: The JSON schema remains TS-compatible with optional server only.
If server_name is removed, parsing/tests no longer encourage it.
If server_name is retained, tests document it as a legacy hidden alias and all model-facing examples use server.
Invalid non-string server inputs produce stable tool-level errors.

candidate_tasks.title: Add focused TS parity tests for ListMcpResourcesTool
candidate_tasks.objective: Create or update tests that fail on the current Go behavior and pin the TS runtime/output contract before implementation work proceeds.
acceptance: Tests assert all-server resource aggregation from at least two servers.
Tests assert specific-server listing calls resources/list even when tools are cached.
Tests assert top-level output is a JSON array and every resource includes server.
Tests assert servers without resources capability contribute [] without resources/list calls.
Tests assert one failing server does not fail aggregate listing.
Tests assert empty output and unknown-server behavior match the chosen TS-compatible contract.
Tests cover the server vs server_name input-surface decision.
